title: Concrete Bag Calculator – How Many Bags You Need
metaDescription: Concrete bag calculator: enter your slab or footing size and instantly find out how many 40lb, 50lb, 60lb or 80lb bags of concrete you need. Free & accurate.
lede: Enter the size of your slab, footing, or post hole below and instantly see how many 40lb, 50lb, 60lb, or 80lb bags of pre-mix concrete you need to buy.

faq.q: How many 80lb bags of concrete do I need per cubic yard?
faq.a: About 45 bags, since one cubic yard equals 27 cubic feet and each 80lb bag yields roughly 0.6 cubic feet.

faq.q: How much area does a 60lb bag of concrete cover?
faq.a: Roughly 1.35 square feet at a 4-inch slab thickness, since a 60lb bag yields about 0.45 cubic feet of mixed concrete.

faq.q: Should I add extra bags for waste?
faq.a: Yes — most contractors add 5-10% extra for spillage, subgrade unevenness, and rounding.

title: Gravel Calculator – How Many Tons or Yards You Need
metaDescription: Gravel calculator: enter your area and depth to instantly find out how many cubic yards and tons of gravel, crushed stone, or pea gravel you need to order.
lede: Enter your driveway, path, or drainage area dimensions to find out exactly how many cubic yards and tons of gravel to order.

faq.q: How much gravel do I need for a driveway?
faq.a: Most driveways use a 4-6 inch base layer. Multiply your driveway's area by the depth in feet, then divide by 27 to get cubic yards.

faq.q: How many tons is a cubic yard of gravel?
faq.a: About 1.4 tons, though crushed stone, pea gravel, and river rock vary slightly by density.

faq.q: Do I need to compact the gravel?
faq.a: Yes, base layers should be compacted in lifts of 2-4 inches for driveways to prevent settling.

title: Mulch Calculator – How Many Bags or Yards You Need
metaDescription: Mulch calculator: enter your flower bed size and depth to instantly see how many cubic yards or bags of mulch you need to buy for your garden.
lede: Enter your garden bed dimensions and desired depth to find out how many bags or cubic yards of mulch you need.

faq.q: How deep should mulch be?
faq.a: 2-3 inches for flower beds, and 3-4 inches around trees and shrubs for effective weed suppression and moisture retention.

faq.q: How many bags of mulch equal a cubic yard?
faq.a: About 13-14 bags of 2 cubic foot mulch, since 1 cubic yard equals 27 cubic feet.

faq.q: Is bulk or bagged mulch cheaper?
faq.a: Bulk delivery is usually cheaper for areas needing more than about 2 cubic yards; bagged mulch is more convenient for smaller beds.

title: Topsoil Calculator – How Many Yards or Tons You Need
metaDescription: Topsoil calculator: enter your area and depth to instantly find out how many cubic yards and tons of topsoil you need for your lawn or garden bed.
lede: Enter your lawn or garden bed dimensions and desired depth to find out how many cubic yards and tons of topsoil to order.

faq.q: How much topsoil do I need for a new lawn?
faq.a: Typically 4-6 inches spread over the existing grade, though this varies with soil quality and drainage needs.

faq.q: How many tons is a cubic yard of topsoil?
faq.a: Roughly 1.35 tons, though moisture content can shift this figure somewhat.

faq.q: Should I add extra topsoil for settling?
faq.a: Yes, adding 10-15% extra accounts for natural compaction after watering and time.

title: Paver Calculator – How Many Pavers You Need
metaDescription: Paver calculator: enter your patio size and paver dimensions to instantly find out how many pavers you need, including a waste allowance for cuts.
lede: Enter your patio or walkway dimensions plus your paver size to find out exactly how many pavers to order.

faq.q: How much waste allowance should I add for pavers?
faq.a: 10% for simple rectangular layouts, and 15-20% for curved edges, diagonal patterns, or complex borders.

faq.q: What base do I need under pavers?
faq.a: A compacted gravel base of 4-6 inches plus a 1-inch bedding sand layer is standard for most patios and walkways.

faq.q: Do I need polymeric sand for pavers?
faq.a: Yes, polymeric sand fills the joints between pavers and helps lock them in place while resisting weeds and ants.

title: Post Hole Concrete Calculator – Bags Per Hole
metaDescription: Post hole concrete calculator: enter your hole diameter, depth, and number of holes to instantly see how many bags of concrete you need for fence posts.
lede: Enter your fence post hole diameter, depth, and quantity to find out exactly how many bags of concrete to buy.

faq.q: How deep should a fence post hole be?
faq.a: Generally at least 1/3 of the post's above-ground height, and always below your local frost line.

faq.q: How much concrete does one fence post need?
faq.a: For a typical 8-inch diameter, 24-inch deep hole, about 1-2 bags of 80lb pre-mix concrete.

faq.q: Can I use quick-set concrete for fence posts?
faq.a: Yes, many quick-set mixes let you skip pre-mixing water into a wheelbarrow — you pour dry mix into the hole and add water directly.

title: Concrete Slab Cost Calculator – Estimate Your Price
metaDescription: Concrete slab cost calculator: enter your slab size and local ready-mix price to instantly estimate your total materials cost per cubic yard.
lede: Enter your slab dimensions and local ready-mix price per cubic yard to get an instant materials cost estimate.

faq.q: What does ready-mix concrete cost per cubic yard?
faq.a: Prices vary by region, typically $120-180 per cubic yard for standard mix, plus delivery fees.

faq.q: Does this estimate include labor?
faq.a: No, this is a materials-only estimate. Labor for pouring and finishing typically adds $2-8 per square foot.

faq.q: Is bagged or ready-mix concrete cheaper for a slab?
faq.a: Ready-mix is usually cheaper per cubic foot once you need more than about 1 cubic yard of concrete.

title: Drywall Sheet Calculator – How Many Sheets You Need
metaDescription: Drywall sheet calculator: enter your total wall area to instantly find out how many 4x8, 4x10, or 4x12 sheets of drywall you need to buy.
lede: Enter your total wall or ceiling area to find out how many sheets of drywall you need, with a built-in waste allowance.

faq.q: How many square feet does a sheet of drywall cover?
faq.a: A standard 4x8 sheet covers 32 square feet; 4x10 covers 40 sq ft, and 4x12 covers 48 sq ft.

faq.q: How much waste allowance should I add for drywall?
faq.a: 10% is standard for rooms with typical door and window openings; more complex rooms may need 15%.

faq.q: How much joint compound do I need?
faq.a: Roughly 1 gallon of joint compound per 500-1000 square feet of drywall, depending on the number of coats.

title: Paint Coverage Calculator – How Many Gallons You Need
metaDescription: Paint coverage calculator: enter your wall area, coats, and paint's coverage rate to instantly find out how many gallons or quarts you need.
lede: Enter your wall area and number of coats to find out exactly how many gallons of paint to buy.

faq.q: How much wall area does a gallon of paint cover?
faq.a: Typically 350-400 square feet per coat on smooth drywall, though textured or porous surfaces cover less.

faq.q: How many coats of paint do I need?
faq.a: Two coats is standard for most color changes; three coats may be needed for dark colors or unprimed surfaces.

faq.q: Should I buy extra paint for touch-ups?
faq.a: Yes, buying one extra quart is common practice for future touch-ups and matching color later.

title: Sod Calculator – How Many Pallets or Pieces You Need
metaDescription: Sod calculator: enter your lawn dimensions to instantly find out how many pallets or individual pieces of sod you need to order for your yard.
lede: Enter your lawn's length and width to find out how many pallets or individual pieces of sod to order.

faq.q: How much sod is on one pallet?
faq.a: Typically 450-500 square feet per pallet, though this varies slightly by sod farm.

faq.q: How soon after delivery should sod be installed?
faq.a: Ideally within 24-48 hours of harvest to prevent it from drying out or overheating in the roll.

faq.q: How much extra sod should I order?
faq.a: About 5% extra covers trimming waste around curves and edges.
